title: Home says when a task in flight has been sent back as a conflict more than once, and how many times
prompt:
Read web/src/home.ts (`missionsToday`, `InFlight`, `sendBacks`), web/src/components/home/Home.tsx (the mission rows' in-flight lines) and web/src/missions.ts (a task's `stages`).

The problem. Roadmap item 8 (sync/roadmap-effects.md, "Next": "A task sent back as a conflict more than once says so on Home", compute). On Home a mission's row lists its tasks in flight with a state ("sent back", "gating") and one "last sent back" line. Nothing says that a task has already lost two or three rounds to conflicts. On the live `/api/missions` (read-only, 2026-11-12), nine tasks of mission 4 were sent back as a conflict two or three times: T106 over 29.9 h, and T113 over 23.6 h before it was cancelled. Three in four conflict send-backs come from owner pushes onto a running task's files (roadmap compute item 7), and each one spends a full worker round and a gate run again. The verdicts are already in the answer (`stages[]`, `stage` "gated", `verdict` "conflict"), but missionsToday reads them only for the row's latest send-back.

Required behaviour.
(a) Every `InFlight` row of `missionsToday` carries:
- `conflicts`: the number of the task's gate verdicts that were `conflict` (a `rejected` or `incompatible` one does not count);
- `conflictText`: "sent back <n> times as a conflict" when there were two or more, else null.
(b) Home's in-flight line shows `conflictText` beside the task's state, in a tone that stands out.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/069.sh. Control records are folded by `spawn_control_refold()`, and `spawn serve` answers `GET /api/missions`. Gate mission 1 holds:
- T1: three conflicts, now sent back;
- T2: a conflict and then a rejection, now gating;
- T3: two conflicts, now gating;
- T4: two incompatible verdicts, now sent back;
- T5: three conflicts and then landed, so it is not in flight.
- (1) Under node, missionsToday's in-flight rows for mission 1 are T1 {conflicts 3, "sent back 3 times as a conflict"}, T2 {1, null}, T3 {2, "sent back 2 times as a conflict"} and T4 {0, null}.
It fails with 1 on 101077e2: the rows carry no `conflicts`.

The product reason. A task that keeps colliding is the clearest sign of wasted fleet work, worker rounds and gate time spent again on the same change. Most of those collisions come from the owner's own pushes. Saying so on the task's line on Home lets the owner see why a task is slow, and hold or finish a push before a task loses a third round.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/, web/test/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green and add tests of your own for the new behaviour: web/test tests for (a) (a task with none, one, two conflicts; rejected and incompatible verdicts not counted; a reviewed send-back not counted) and for (b) (the line showing the text).
